facts.statement: The genus Nanuqsaurus contains only one species, Nanuqsaurus hoglundi, which is known from a partial skull and various postcranial and tooth fragments.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Nanuqsaurus hoglundi, known from a partial skull and multiple undescribed postcranial and teeth elements.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Nanuqsaurus were discovered in 2006 at the Kikak-Tegoseak Quarry in the North Slope Borough of Alaska.
facts.quote: In 2006, within the North Slope Borough of Alaska, the fossilized remains of a medium-sized theropod were located at the Kikak-Tegoseak Quarry of the Prince Creek Formation.

facts.statement: The genus Nanuqsaurus was formally described and named by Anthony R. Fiorillo and Ronald S. Tykoski in 2014.
facts.quote: This prompted the creation of a new genus, Nanuqsaurus, described and named by Anthony R. Fiorillo and Ronald S. Tykoski in 2014.

facts.statement: The name Nanuqsaurus combines the Iñupiaq word 'nanuq' for polar bear and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The type species, Nanuqsaurus hoglundi, has its generic name derived from the Iñupiaq word for 'polar bear', nanuq, and the Greek word , meaning 'lizard'.

facts.statement: Recent studies of additional fossils suggest Nanuqsaurus was likely similar in size to large North American tyrannosaurids like Albertosaurus, rather than being a small animal as initially thought.
facts.quote: However, later studies tied 13 additional fossil elements across a 20 km stretch of the Colville River to a single theropod taxon. Further, that more recent work suggested that its supposed small size was unfounded and that it was likely similar in size to other North American tyrannosaurids, such as Albertosaurus which grew up to 8 - 9 m long, based on undescribed adult-sized teeth and postcranial elements.

facts.statement: Some postcranial elements of Nanuqsaurus scale to approximately 7 meters in length, comparable to a juvenile Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: Some of the undescribed postcranial elements scale to around 7 m in length, described comparable to a juvenile Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Based on recently collected fossils, adult Nanuqsaurus specimens are estimated to have weighed over 1.9 metric tons.
facts.quote: It is estimated that the adult Nanuqsaurus specimens would have weighed over 1.9 MT based on these recently collected fossils.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus lived during the latest Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Nanuqsaurus hoglundi, known from a partial skull and multiple undescribed postcranial and teeth elements.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus lived between 70 and 68 million years ago at the beginning of the Maastrichtian stage in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Nanuqsaurus hoglundi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Nanuqsaurus (que significa "lagarto oso polar"), un dinosaurio terópodo tiranosáurido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, entre 70 a 68 millones de años, a principios del Maastrichtiano, en lo que ahora es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Nanuqsaurus remained in the paleo-Arctic year-round, enduring approximately 120 days of constant winter darkness without migrating.
facts.quote: This evidence suggests that both Nanuqsaurus and its likely prey items remained in the paleo-Arctic yearlong and would have had to cope with ~120 days of constant winter darkness each year, as opposed to resorting to migration to escape the harsh conditions.

facts.statement: It is proposed that Nanuqsaurus laid eggs around April to take advantage of the constant daylight and relative warmth for incubation.
facts.quote: It is proposed that the animals would likely have laid their eggs toward the beginning of the constant daylight period, around the month of April, allowing time for the eggs to incubate in the relative heat of this part of the year.

facts.statement: As the largest carnivore in its area, Nanuqsaurus was likely an apex predator.
facts.quote: As the largest carnivore in its area it was most likely an apex predator.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Nanuqsaurus as a close relative of Daspletosaurus and Tyrannosaurus within the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis of Tyrannosauridae finds Nanuqsaurus to be a close relative of Daspletosaurus and Tyrannosaurus within Tyrannosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2023 thesis argued that Nanuqsaurus is a nomen dubium due to poorly resolved taxonomic validity and phylogenetic position.
facts.quote: A 2023 thesis argued that its taxonomic validity and phylogenetic position is poorly resolved, and that the taxon is a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Further studies have indicated that the anatomical traits used to diagnose Nanuqsaurus may not be unique to the genus.
facts.quote: However, further studies have indicated that these anatomical traits may not be diagnostic.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the rostral parietal spur is actually present in Nanuqsaurus, as this trait is variably present across Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: The first two dentary teeth being smaller than those behind is variably present throughout Tyrannosauridae and the actual presence of the rostral parietal spur is debatable.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus was estimated to be about 6 meters long, roughly half the length of a Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado la longitud de Nanuqsaurus en cerca de 6 metros de largo, aproximadamente la mitad de la longitud de Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: Its weight was estimated to be between 500 and 900 kilograms.
facts.quote: Su peso se ha estimado entre 500 a 900 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The reconstructed skull length, based on proportions of its close relatives, is 60 to 70 centimeters.
facts.quote: La longitud del cráneo reconstruido, basándose en las proporciones de sus parientes cercanos, es de 60–70 centímetros.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus has a distinctive edge on its head indicating it was closely related to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Nanuqsaurus tiene un borde de forma particular en su cabeza indicando que estaba emparentado de cerca con Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: As a tyrannosaurine, it is diagnosed by a thin, bifurcated midline rostral process of fused parietals overlapping the frontals, elongated rostral frontals separating prefrontal and lacrimal facets, and the first two dentary teeth being much smaller than the following ones.
facts.quote: Clasificado como un tiranosaurino, Nanuqsaurus es diagnosticado por: un espolón medio, delgado y bifurcado rostralmente, de los parietales fusionados en la parte dorsal de la bóveda craneana que se solapa y separa a los frontales dentro de la cresta sagital; los frontales con un proceso largo y ahusado rostralmente que separa a las facetas de los huesos prefrontal y lacrimal; y los dos primeros dientes del dentario son mucho más pequeños que los que le siguen.

facts.statement: Its fossil remains, a partial skull with jaw, were found in the Prince Creek Formation in northern Alaska.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles, un cráneo parcial con mandíbula, han aparecido en la Formación Prince Creek en el norte de Alaska.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus was first described and named by Anthony R. Fiorillo and Ronald S. Tykoski in 2014.
facts.quote: Nanuqsaurus fue descrito y nombrado inicialmente por Anthony R. Fiorillo y Ronald S. Tykoski en 2014.

facts.statement: The name is derived from the Iñupiaq word nanuq, meaning "polar bear".
facts.quote: El nombre se deriva de la palabra Iñupiaq nanuq, que significa "oso polar".

facts.statement: The species name honors philanthropist Forrest Hoglund.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra al filántropo Forrest Hoglund.

facts.statement: The holotype, DMNH 21461, was found in a layer of the Prince Creek Formation dated to 69.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, DMNH 21461, ha sido hallado en una capa de la Formación Prince Creek, datada en 69.1 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype includes the right nasal ramus of the maxilla, a partial cranial vault with parietal, frontal, and right laterosphenoid pieces, and the front of the left dentary.
facts.quote: Este abarca el ramo nasal del maxilar derecho; una bóveda craneana parcial que incluye piezas del los parietales, frontales y un lateroesfenoides derecho; y el frente del dentario izquierdo.

facts.statement: The Kikak-Tegoseak Quarry region of the Prince Creek Formation dates to the late early Maastrichtian, 71 to 68 million years ago.
facts.quote: A una edad de 71–68 millones de años , la región de la cantera Kikak-Tegoseak de la Formación Prince Creek data de principios del Maastrichtiense tardío.

facts.statement: An average age of 69.1 ± 0.3 million years found in the formation rocks suggests Nanuqsaurus lived at that time.
facts.quote: Una edad promedio encontrada en las rocas que datan de la formación es de 69.1 ± 0.3 millones de años atrás, por lo que es probable que Nanuqsaurus sea de esa edad.

facts.statement: It is one of the few dinosaurs known to live in very high latitude zones.
facts.quote: Es uno de los pocos dinosaurios que viven en zonas de muy altas latitudes.

facts.statement: Its time range is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Paleontologists suggest that about 70 million years ago, northern Alaska was separated from the continent of Laramidia and experienced a cold climate with long periods of darkness and light, making food hard to find.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con los paleontólogos, hace unos 70 millones de años el norte de Alaska estaba apartado del antiguo subcontinente llamado Laramidia y experimentaba un clima frío y largos períodos de oscuridad y de luz, en adición a las estaciones en las cuales la comida no sería fácil de encontrar.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus likely decreased in size due to a year-round decrease in food supply caused by colder temperatures.
facts.quote: Nanuqsaurus probablemente disminuyó de tamaño debido a la disminución en el suministro de alimentos durante todo el año, causado por las temperaturas más frías.

facts.statement: The shape of its skull suggests it had an enlarged brain area dedicated to smell, indicating it relied heavily on scent to hunt prey, similar to Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: La forma de su cráneo sugiere que tenía un área agrandada del cerebro dedicada al olfato, lo que sugiere que el animal dependía fuertemente del olor para cazar a sus presas, al igual que Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: Given its size and cold environment, it is probable that Nanuqsaurus hoglundi was covered in a layer of hair-like feathers, as known in other tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: Es probable que, dados su tamaño y el ambiente frío en que vivió, Nanuqsaurus hoglundi estuviera cubierto de una capa de plumas similares a pelo, como es conocidos en otros tiranosauroideos.

facts.statement: Nanuqsaurus is a member of the highly derived tyrannosaurine subfamily.
facts.quote: Nanuqsaurus es un miembro de la subfamilia de los tiranosaurinos sumamente derivado.

facts.statement: It is considered the sister taxon to a clade containing Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and probably Zhuchengtyrannus.
facts.quote: Se considera que es el taxón hermano de un clado que contiene a Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus, y probablemente a Zhuchengtyrannus.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Tyrannosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosaurinae

facts.statement: It belongs to the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Tyrannosauridae

facts.statement: It is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: However, later studies suggest its supposed small size was not well-founded and that it was probably similar in size to other North American tyrannosaurids such as Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios posteriores sugieren que su supuesto tamaño pequeño no estaba bien fundamentado, y que probablemente era muy similar en tamaño a otros tiranosáuridos norteamericanos tales como Albertosaurus.
